Resolves #22026

Related: #21033

Refreshes only the Engine E2E duration table from five successful full `dev` push matrices. On the previously red `24e82335fe` run, the held-out replay moves the slowest shard from **365.3 s to 327.6 s** of observed test time, with each of the 322 specs still scheduled once. The ordinary full PR matrix verifies the refreshed schedule at 15 shards and the existing 360 s limit.

Evidence: L3 (the exact PR’s full hosted Engine matrix, measured replay of held-out hosted logs, and local selector tests). The cut’s merged `dev` readback remains owned by #21033.

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — generated timing data only.

- **Change class:** restoration. The timing table recalibrates the existing balancer.
- **Prescription checked:** `buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json` is the data consumed by the current shard balancer. The slowest spec’s existing weight already matches the measured run.
- **Preflight:** local selector suite passed. Agent preflight is not hosted in Engine. The hosted baseline runs on the PR.

## Test Evidence

`e2eCiSelection.mjs --engine-durations` takes the costliest observed time per spec. The training inputs were five green full dev pushes. The current red push supplied the held-out costs. [Run 1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45093630484) · [Run 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45092634092) · [Run 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45083025229) · [Run 4](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45082083901) · [Run 5](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45079273939) · [Held-out run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821)

The selector's fixture cases ran with their own temporary indexes. Its three real-tree cases used an index verified against all 7,508 paths on the current dev base. The change selected `full`.

The first full repair run passed 14 shards. Shard 10 reported 102 of 104 test results with zero assertion failures before its deadline. The completed `ExamplesCatalogTheme` cases took 99.3 s against 65.5 s recorded, and the completed `ApplicationToolbarNL` cases took 16.3 s against 2.8 s. The follow-up uses those observations. The original red dev replay now estimates 320.7 s for the slowest shard. The first PR replay estimates 317.6 s, using the previous budget for the final unmeasured spec. [Initial full run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45112918521)
